clue.text: Bolshie member of cast who alters the script?

parts.note: Bolshie (Bolshevik) means left-wing, Communist, which is red
a member of a play's cast is an actor

explanation.surface: A truculent performer who takes it upon themselves to rewrite their lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor is an editor, someone who revises and prepares a text for publication.

clue.text: People get a move on

definitions.meaning: a people or nation sharing descent

explanation.definitionFit: Race means both an ethnic group of people and, as a verb, to rush along.

clue.text: Get behind bore

definitions.meaning: to lag or trail behind others

explanation.definitionFit: Drag means to trail along slowly, and in slang a drag is a tiresome bore.

clue.text: Lure using trick outside someone's 'ouse

indicators.note: outside says the word for trick goes round the other piece

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
home with its H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'ouse shows, is 'OME

explanation.surface: Tempting someone with a ruse to get into their house, written in Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ouse tells you to drop the H from HOME too.
explanation.definitionFit: A come-on is an enticement or inducement, something meant to draw a person in.

clue.text: Like some races — it's obvious the man can't move

parts.note: something that sticks is stuck fast and cannot move

explanation.surface: A remark about a man plainly unable to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: The STICKS are the fences or hurdles of jump racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeplechases and hurdle races are run over the sticks, meaning over jumps.

clue.text: Snake? The man's only half calm

parts.note: his means belonging to the man

indicators.note: only half says just the first part of the word for calm is used

explanation.surface: A question about a snake, then the remark that a man is only partly composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps SER, the first half of SERENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake hisses, so whimsically it is a hisser; the question mark flags this playful sense.

clue.text: Bound to be Indian tea in pubs

indicators.note: in says the tea is put inside the word for pubs

parts.note: chai is the Hindi word for tea, spiced Indian tea

explanation.surface: A claim that someone is fated to drink Indian tea in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bound is tied up or fettered, as a prisoner in chains is.

clue.text: Unique genius is exceptional, without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the jumbled letters go round the hesitation
exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that a remarkable genius is someone who never falters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense of outside it wraps the scrambled genius-plus-is around the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Sui generis is Latin for of its own kind, unique, in a class of its own.

clue.text: English place in part establishing good name

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for part

parts.note: a ration is a portion or share

explanation.surface: An English venue playing its part in building a fine reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputation is a person's standing or name, so a good name is a good reputation.

clue.text: Conservative safe, but lacking allure

explanation.surface: A Tory who is a safe pair of hands but has no charisma.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is allure, so something without charm is lacking allure.

clue.text: Devour the last of eggs, say — cooked now

definitions.text: Devour the last of eggs, say — cooked now

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared and mixed, so the letters are rearranged
last of says only the final letter of eggs is taken

explanation.surface: An urging to eat up the egg dish being prepared right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes pancake day, when eggs are cooked and eaten; S is the last of 'eggs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, Pancake Day, is when eggs are used up in pancakes before Lent.

clue.text: Firm's difficult time is being denied by president

indicators.note: being denied says the word is taken away from the difficult time

parts.note: a crisis is a difficult time

explanation.surface: A company's troubled period that a president refuses to acknowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Firm is 'is', a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp means firm and brittle, as a fresh apple or biscuit is.

clue.text: Guardian changed after Preston

indicators.note: changed says the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's guardian altered following a move to Preston, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a position indicator but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A foster parent is a guardian who brings up a child not their own.

clue.text: Gang coming in like wine to be sharp

indicators.note: coming in says the gang goes inside the word for wine

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine
a ring is a gang, as of criminals

explanation.surface: A gang arriving, and the wine turning sour.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent means sharp or biting, as a harsh comment or a tart taste is.

clue.text: Working at clue, my aim (without taking years!) is to be perfect

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A setter explaining their ambition while working on a clue: to be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without taking' removes the Y of years from the pool before the letters of AT CLUE MY AIM are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate means flawless, spotless, without fault.

clue.text: One wrestling with problem — something that can't be squared!

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O is a circle, which famously cannot be squared

explanation.surface: Someone grappling with an impossible problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaring the circle is the classic impossible task, so the circle is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling, and the word also names a sumo wrestler.

clue.text: Archdeacon's aim mostly to be be surrounded by warmth of a divine nature

indicators.note: surrounded by says these pieces go inside the word for warmth

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon; with the 's it gives VENS

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the aim is dropped

explanation.surface: A churchman's goal being enveloped in warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts END to EN. 'be be' is a printed slip; both are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven-sent means coming as if from heaven, providential, so divine in origin.

clue.text: Act in which alcoholic drink is banished

indicators.note: in which says the drink sits inside the act

explanation.surface: A stage act in which booze is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deported is to be expelled from a country, banished.

clue.text: Hesitation about having booze served at front of gallery buildings

indicators.note: about says the hesitation word is turned around
at front says only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Uncertainty over drinks being handed out at the entrance to an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ER into RE; 'at front' takes S from served.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is property in land and buildings.

clue.text: Princess acted to get love

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A princess performing in order to win affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the Tyrian princess who founded Carthage, in Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Second female pop singer, one to flower

parts.note: Cilla Black was a Liverpool-born British pop singer

explanation.surface: A second female singer is one about to blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a 1960s British pop star and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scilla is a genus of bulbous plants, the squills, with blue flowers.

clue.text: Medical knowhow cures niece? No, sadly!

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone asks if treatments will heal a niece, and is told regretfully not.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuroscience is the science of the nervous system, a branch of medical knowledge.

clue.text: A big landowner one is opposing

parts.note: NT, the National Trust, is one of Britain's largest landowners
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wealthy landowner who is against something.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British heritage charity owning vast estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against, opposing.

clue.text: I had left foot hidden in bed?

parts.note: I'd is short for I had

indicators.note: hidden says the abbreviation for foot is taken out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone says they kept their left foot tucked under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it removes FT from LEFT, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in bed suggests being inactive, lazing about, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Last bit of the agreement is a matter of astronomical significance

indicators.note: last bit of says the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: The closing part of a treaty proves hugely important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astronomical' suggests huge, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epact is the moon's age at the start of the year, used in calendar reckoning.

clue.text: What the substitutes are when the team gets stuffed

parts.note: lined means filled, as a lined stomach is stuffed

explanation.surface: A football team that eats too much, with the subs watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Substitutes not playing sit on the bench at the edge of the pitch, out of action.

clue.text: Cool attempt to get across border

indicators.note: to get across says the attempt spans the border, around it

parts.note: an end is a border or limit

explanation.surface: A stylish attempt to cross a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, which is a sense of cool.

clue.text: Sound of girl, a little child, is hot stuff

indicators.note: sound of says the following words are said aloud

parts.note: Dinah is a girl's name; a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A small girl turns out to be a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is an explosive, and in slang hot stuff, something sensational.
